info.title: chainmail API
info.description:
Read-only HTTP over a local chainmail corpus: search for candidate chains, choose which belong on a page, then build the timeline spec the renderer consumes.

Two stages on purpose. Search selects; POST /v1/spec renders a chosen set. A spec built straight from a query takes whatever the query returned, and then the only way to remove a thread is to regenerate the page.

This serves personal mail and has no authentication of any kind. It binds to loopback and refuses a non-loopback address unless explicitly overridden, and spec bodies carry unsanitised sender HTML (issue #14) — so the loopback bind is what makes the whole surface safe, not a default to be relaxed.

Operator commands — ingest, embed, eval, dedupe, twins, repair, merge, alias, refresh — are deliberately absent. They mutate the corpus and belong to the CLI.

servers.description: The only supported deployment: loopback on the machine holding the corpus.

get.summary: Ranked chains for a query — the selection candidates.
get.description:
Selection stage. Lexical by default: FTS5 wins decisively on the tokens a mail corpus is dense with (invoice numbers, account ids, Message-IDs), and the structural half of a real question is a filter rather than something a similarity score encodes.

At least one of q, person or since must be given. With no filter at all an arbitrary slice of the corpus would come back reading like a ranked answer, so that is a 400.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free text. Double-quoted runs are kept as phrases; every other term must match. Terms that look like identifiers also go to the trigram index.

parameters.name: person
parameters.description: An address, display name or Slack uid. Matches anyone recorded on the entry, author or recipient — on a real trail a quarter of the participants appear only in to:/cc:, so "threads Ada was on" cannot be an author-only filter.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only entries on or after this date.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Retrieval. semantic and hybrid need vectors (`corpus embed`) AND a running local embedding daemon; without the daemon they return 503, never an empty result set.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many chains (or entries) to return.

parameters.name: entries
parameters.description: Return the matching entries instead of the chains they belong to. Changes which array of the response is populated.

400.description: No filter given, or a parameter could not be parsed.

503.description: mode=semantic or mode=hybrid, and the embedding daemon is not reachable or has not pulled the model. The message names the fix.

504.description: The embedding daemon did not answer in time.

post.summary: Build a timeline spec from a chosen set of chains.
post.description:
Render stage, and deliberately separate from search: what belongs on a page is a human decision, and removing a thread afterwards means regenerating everything downstream, so scope is settled once, up front.

The response validates against schema/timeline.schema.json, the contract the renderer already consumes.

Expensive: spec assembly recovers quoted bodies, detects repeated boilerplate and builds attachment thumbnails, which is seconds for a large selection. There is no job queue — the response is synchronous. Concurrency is capped, so an over-eager caller gets 429 rather than a server with every core in HTML recovery.

Entry bodies are sender HTML, and it is NOT sanitised (issue #14). That is accepted at today's risk because the server binds to loopback only. It is a hard blocker on binding wider, not a footnote.

200.description: A timeline spec, valid against schema/timeline.schema.json.

400.description: Malformed body, an empty chains list, or a selection that resolved to no entries.

404.description: One of the named chains is not in the corpus. The message names which.

429.description: Too many spec builds already in flight. Retry-After is set.

get.summary: A page that POST /v1/spec saved under a name — the read half of the render route /view/<name>.
get.description: The page was written by the same server process family (specs live beside the corpus, in ~/.local/state/chainmail/specs), so a refresh or a reboot lands back on the same page from the same URL. The response is byte-identical to what the build returned.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name the build was saved under. Letters, digits, '.', '_', '-'; no slashes and no '..'.

400.description: The name is not a valid spec name.

404.description: No page was ever saved under that name.

get.summary: One entry, with its provenance and every sighting of it.

parameters.name: extId
parameters.description: Corpus natural key, as search reports it. Percent-encode it: it contains a colon and usually angle brackets.

404.description: No entry carries that id. Distinct from a search that matched nothing, which is a 200 with an empty array.

get.summary: The chain around an entry, in time order, as data.
get.description:
Kept even though selection makes it unnecessary for building a page, because reading a chain is a different act from rendering one: a client browsing a candidate wants its entries as data, cheaply, without paying for spec assembly or committing to a page.

Reachability is followed in BOTH directions, so ANY member's ext id returns the whole conversation — search reports the entry that matched, not the root. The parameter is named rootExtId because that is what search hands you.

parameters.name: rootExtId
parameters.description: Ext id of any entry in the chain. Percent-encode it.

get.summary: Everyone in the corpus, with their identities.

post.summary: Bring a previously built page up to date.
post.description:
Refresh stage, and deliberately the read half of the CLI's `refresh` command. The caller posts the previous spec (as POST /v1/spec returned it) and any selection overrides; the server re-derives the page from the corpus — a chain already on the page that gained entries is grown, a new chain the recorded queries find is proposed rather than included — and returns the regenerated spec alongside a report of what changed.

The server never reaches the mailbox, on purpose: fetching what arrived is `corpus ingest`'s job and belongs to the CLI and the cron, not a browser. So this refresh is corpus-only. What it cannot see, it cannot propose from fed to it by the mailbox later.

200.description: The refreshed spec and what the refresh did.

400.description: Malformed body, a spec with no messages, or a spec version this build cannot reproduce.

SearchResponse.description: Ranked candidates. Exactly one of chains or entries is present, decided by the `entries` parameter; neither is present when nothing matched, and an empty array is returned rather than omitted in that case.

ChainHit.description: One candidate chain — the unit a caller selects for POST /v1/spec.

rootExtId.description: Ext id of the entry the reply graph terminates at. The only chain identity worth storing, and what POST /v1/spec takes.

subject.description: Subject of the chain. Absent when no entry in it carries one.

container.description: Mail thread id or Slack channel id. Absent when the source stated none.

sources.description: Every archive this chain has entries from; more than one where a mail trail continued in Slack.

matched.description: How many of them the query hit. matched/entries is the honest measure of whether the chain is about the query.

first.description: Timestamp of the earliest entry, UTC.

last.description: Timestamp of the latest entry, UTC.

score.description: Fused score. Comparable within one response only.

best.description: The top-scoring entries of this chain, most relevant first — the evidence for the ranking.

EntryHit.description: One matching entry, as ranking sees it.

extId.description: Corpus natural key, e.g. "mail:<c0ffee-1@example.com>". The identity that survives a rebuild, and the one the other endpoints take.

personId.description: Author's person id, 0 when the author could not be resolved.

person.description: Author's display name. Absent when no person row is attached.

container.description: Mail thread id or Slack channel id. Absent when the source stated none.

subject.description: Absent for sources that have no subject, such as Slack.

permalink.description: Opens the entry at its source. Absent when the source gave none.

snippet.description: Match excerpt with matched terms wrapped in square brackets. Absent for a structural-only query, which has nothing to highlight.

score.description: Fused Reciprocal Rank Fusion score. Comparable within one response only.

proseRank.description: 1-based position in the prose ranking; 0 means that ranking did not find this entry. Always present, because 0 is meaningful.

identRank.description: 1-based position in the identifier (trigram) ranking; 0 means it did not find this entry.

semRank.description: 1-based position in the vector ranking; 0 means it did not find this entry, and is always 0 for mode=lexical.

similarity.description: Cosine to the query vector, in [-1, 1]. Present only when semRank is non-zero; it is reported, not fused.

CorpusEntry.description: One entry resolved for reading rather than for ranking: plain text, with its provenance. Deliberately not a timeline entry — no HTML recovery, no boilerplate folding, no thumbnails — so reading a chain costs a query rather than seconds of assembly. Use POST /v1/spec when the goal is to render.

quoted.description: True when this entry exists only because someone quoted it: it was never in the mailbox as a standalone message.

tz.description: Zone label as the source stated it, e.g. "NZST". Absent when the source stated none; never guessed here.

tzOffsetMinutes.description: Minutes east of UTC as the source stated it. Absent when it stated none. Carried alongside tz because a label does not determine an offset.

author.description: Display name of the sender. Absent when no person row is attached.

subject.description: Absent for sources that have no subject.

body.description: The entry's own plain text. Absent when the source carried no text body.

container.description: Mail thread id or Slack channel id. Absent when the source stated none.

permalink.description: Opens the entry at its source. Absent when the source gave none.

parent.description: Ext id of the entry this replies to. Absent at a chain root, and also absent when it names a parent that is not in the corpus — parentRef tells the two apart.

parentRef.description: What the entry names as its parent (a Message-ID or thread_ts), resolved or not. Present with no parent means a known hole.

sightings.description: Every place this entry was found.

participants.description: Everyone recorded on it, senders first.

ChainResponse.description: Every entry reachable from the named one, in time order.

rootExtId.description: The id that was asked for, echoed back. Note this is whatever the caller passed, which need not be the chain's root — see the path parameter.

entries.description: The whole chain in time order, never empty: an id that resolves to nothing is a 404.

Sighting.description: One place an entry was found. A message quoted in five forwards has five, which is the evidence that it mattered.

seenIn.description: Ext id of the message it was found inside. Absent for a direct sighting, which was not found inside anything.

detail.description: Free-text note about the sighting. Absent when none was recorded.

Participant.description: Someone recorded on an entry, in role order.

role.description: How they appear on this entry.

SpecRequest.description: A page built from a chosen set of chains. Selection is the caller's decision and is not re-derived from a query here: naming chains IS the selection step.

chains.description: Chain roots to include, as GET /v1/search reports them. At least one; an empty list is a 400, because a page with no messages fails the timeline schema.

title.description: Page title. Defaults to the subject of the earliest selected entry, which the timeline schema requires to be non-empty.

me.description: The reader's own addresses, so their outbound messages are marked. Nothing in the corpus knows which mailbox it was collected from.

items.description: One of the reader's own addresses.

queries.description: The searches the selection came from, recorded on the page so that a hole in the timeline is interpretable. Purely descriptive: nothing is re-run.

name.description: When set, saves the built page under /view/<name> so it survives a refresh (and a reboot) and can be reopened from its URL. The client chooses it; the server validates it. Letters, digits, '.', '_', '-'; no slashes and no '..'. Blank builds without saving.

SpecQuery.description: A search that was run, recorded for provenance.

note.description: Where it was run, e.g. "corpus search".

Stats.description: What is in the corpus, and what is missing.

people.description: Distinct people, senders and recipients alike.

chainRoots.description: Entries that open a chain: no parent, and none named.

unresolved.description: Entries that name a parent which is not in the corpus. Known holes, not errors.

embeddings.description: Empty when nothing has been embedded, in which case mode=semantic and mode=hybrid have nothing to rank against.

EmbedModelStats.description: Embedding coverage for one model. Reported per model because a half-finished model migration is a real state, and from the results alone it looks like a corpus that lost recall.

skipped.description: Entries deliberately not embedded, as having no topic.

stale.description: Stored, but the entry's text or the preparation has moved on since.

eligible.description: Entries a full backfill would still embed — how much work is left.

PeopleResponse.description: Everyone in the corpus, most involved first.

PersonSummary.description: One person, with every identity that resolves to them.

identities.description: Every address or uid folded into this person.

received.description: Entries they were a to: or cc: on. Sent 0 with received above 0 is a recipient-only participant, which is a quarter of a real cast.

RefreshRequest.description: The previous run being brought up to date. The spec itself is authoritative for what stays on the page; the other fields narrow or rename how that membership is reproduced, and accept takes proposed chains the report returns.

spec.description: The previous spec, as POST /v1/spec returned it. Must carry at least one message; a fresh page has nothing to refresh.

person.description: Address, name or slack uid, overriding the spec's recorded selection.

since.description: YYYY-MM-DD floor on entry dates, overriding the spec's recorded selection.

limit.description: How many chains a query may propose, overriding the spec's recorded selection.

me.description: The reader's own addresses, so their outbound messages are marked.

items.description: One of the reader's own addresses.

includeNew.description: Accept every chain the queries propose, without naming them one by one. Defaults to false: a curated page is not re-widened on every refresh.

accept.description: Chain roots to accept, as the report's chainsProposed names them. Accepting is idempotent: a chain accepted once is not proposed again.

items.description: A rootExtId as the report prints it.

RefreshResponse.description: The regenerated spec, plus a report of what the refresh did to get there. The spec is what a client renders; the report is what it shows to explain a change.

RefreshReport.description: What moved between the previous run and this one. A chain is in exactly one list: added (new to the page), grown (was there and gained entries), proposed (found but not accepted) or unranked (kept, but its query no longer finds it).

entriesBefore.description: Messages on the page when the refresh started.

entriesAfter.description: Messages on the page after the refresh.

chainsAdded.description: Chains now on the page that were not on it before. Absent when none.

chainsGrown.description: Chains on the page before that gained entries. Absent when none.

chainsProposed.description: Chains a recorded query found that the page does not include, awaiting a decision. Accept them with the next refresh's accept.

chainsUnranked.description: Chains still on the page that no recorded query returns anymore. They are kept — dropping one would delete entries somebody has already read.

nothingNew.description: The refresh looked and found nothing to store, grow, add or propose. Distinct from an error: a report existing at all means the refresh actually ran.

ChainGrowth.description: One chain whose membership changed. before is absent when the chain is new to the page; after is what the page now holds.

id.description: The chain's container id (a Gmail thread id or Slack channel id).

subject.description: Subject of the chain, when it carries one.

before.description: Entries the chain had before. Absent when it is new to the page.

RefreshCandidate.description: A chain the queries found that the page does not yet include, named by the id that accepts it.

rootExtId.description: The chain root to pass back as accept, as GET /v1/search reports it.

subject.description: Subject of the chain, when it carries one.

container.description: Mail thread id or Slack channel id.

matched.description: How many of them the query hit. matched/entries is the honest measure of whether it is about the query.

span.description: Earliest – latest dates, e.g. '2 Jan 2026 – 14 Mar 2026'.

Error.description: Every non-2xx response carries this and nothing else.

error.description: What went wrong, in the same words the CLI would use. Written to be shown to a person.
error.example: mode "semantic": no embedding daemon reachable at http://localhost:11434: start it with `ollama serve`

TimelineSpec.title: Timeline
TimelineSpec.description: One email trail, unspooled out of its threads and forwards into a single chronological transcript. Produced by a collector (e.g. the mail-timeline skill); consumed by the chainmail renderer.

title.description: Page title. A leading # renders as a channel-style hash.

subtitle.description: One or two sentences. Provenance belongs in queries/threads/sourceNotes, not here.

runLabel.description: Names this collection pass, e.g. 'pass 2, 20 Aug 2026'.

runs.description: Labels of every pass so far, oldest first.

openItems.description: Unresolved questions, commitments and ownerless decisions. HTML permitted; cross-links encouraged.

avatars.description: Sender name -> image (data: URI or URL). Keys must match Message.sender exactly.

participants.description: The full cast, including people who only ever appear as recipients.

email.description: Omit when no address appears anywhere in the trail. Never guess one.

note.description: Use instead of role for cc-only people and aliases.

runParams.description: Selection parameters this run was invoked with, so a later refresh reproduces the same page. Only what the rest of the spec cannot already supply; never a machine-local path.

me.description: Addresses belonging to the reader, whose messages render as outbound.

limit.description: How many chains the search was allowed to select.

person.description: Address, name or slack uid the selection was filtered to.

queries.description: Searches run, so a null result is interpretable.

threads.description: Mail threads the transcript was assembled from.

id.description: Gmail thread or message id; links out.

sourceNotes.description: Provenance caveats: avatar sources, unrecoverable addresses, truncation.

kind.description: 'note' is a meeting or event that never existed as an email.

id.description: Stable anchor. Omit to derive from date+time+sender; content-derived ids survive inserting entries mid-trail.

date.description: As displayed, e.g. 'Thu 16 Jul 2026'. Not normalised.

time.description: As displayed, e.g. '11:35'. Absent for undated notes.

tz.description: The zone this entry's clock is in, e.g. 'NZST', '+0530'. Drives absolute-time ordering. Omit rather than guess: absent means the zone is unknown and the renderer shows it as unknown.

tzSource.description: Where tz came from. 'stated' is the source's own Date header or zone label. 'inferred' was worked out from other evidence and must be presented as a claim, not a fact. Omit when tz is absent.

org.description: Drives colour, assigned in first-appearance order.

to.description: Free text as it appeared, including 'cc ...'.

subject.description: Names the chain when this entry opens one. Capture it during collection.

label.description: Notes only: what the meeting was.

body.description:
Trusted HTML.

,

    , , ,

    for editorial gloss, for cross-links.

quoted.description: Reconstructed from quoted text; never existed as a standalone message here.

source.description: Where it came from: a Gmail id, or 'unspooled from the 2 Aug email'.

parent.description: Id of the entry this replies to. Absent means it opens a chain. Coverage here drives ordering, lanes and the reply tree.

meta.description: Meeting scheduling exhaust (invitation, notes, accept/decline). Forces the classification the renderer would otherwise infer.

gmailId.description: Links to the message in Gmail. Only ever present on real messages.

link.description: Opens the attachment at its source, for attachments not reached through Gmail.

preview.description: Thumbnail as a data: URI. Never a URL — the page renders without a network.
